message.content: Fusion research has already delivered significant benefits to society in various ways. First, superconducting magnets developed for fusion reactors have advanced medical imaging and particle therapy. Second, plasma physics insights have improved industrial processing and semiconductor manufacturing. Third, fusion testing has driven innovations in materials science that now serve aerospace and energy sectors. The iritic challenge of containing plasma at extreme temperatures has pushed computational modeling far beyond its previous limits, benefiting weather prediction and climate science. These spin-off technologies demonstrate that fusion research pays dividends well before a commercial reactor exists.
